title: Schedule of Checked Baggage Charging Basis — Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
Checked baggage on a booking under Air Ticket Fare Brands is charged bag by bag and traveller by traveller. The bags included in the fare brand are free, and each bag beyond the allowance is charged at the brand's first-bag or second-bag rate by its position in that traveller's own sequence.

|Charge line|When it arises|What is charged|
|---|---|---|
|First checked bag of a traveller|the brand's included checked-bag allowance is at least one bag|nothing|
|First checked bag of a traveller|the brand includes no checked bag in the fare|the brand's first-bag rate|
|Second checked bag of a traveller|the brand's included checked-bag allowance is at least two bags|nothing|
|Second checked bag of a traveller|the brand includes fewer than two checked bags|the brand's second-bag rate|
|A bag over the weight allowance|the bag is heavier than the allowance|the brand's overweight charge|
|A bag over the size allowance|the bag is larger than the allowance|the brand's oversize charge|

**Annotations to the lines above.**

1. Position is taken in each traveller's own sequence of bags, so the first-bag and second-bag lines are read separately for every traveller on the booking.
2. Where a single bag is both over the weight allowance and over the size allowance, the two charges are added rather than the larger of them taken.
3. An optional extra is sold only while the booking record stands at held or ticketed. The status is read from the record of the booking the extra would be sold on, before the charge is raised.
4. Bags bought before the day of departure are charged at the rates in this charter. Bags presented at the airport are the airline's own affair and are never charged here.
5. A bag line already charged was refunded in full where the traveller cancelled the whole itinerary inside the void window, and was otherwise refunded only where the flight itself did not operate. That basis is no longer in force. The other clauses of this sheet stand.
